summary.overview: The project has strong task context through its AGENTS.md, OpenSpec workflow, and six configured Skills, but quality enforcement and delivery acceptance rely entirely on convention without a mechanical gate. Session evidence was unavailable; findings derive from repository-level inspection only.

suggestions.title: Route the bash-defensive-patterns Skill into the next shell-script task
suggestions.reason: It is the only Skill with trigger, procedure, output, and validation present, but it is not routed to any agent task. Exercising it on a bounded script task would confirm its value before extending the Skill set.
suggestions.nextStep: Use the bash-defensive-patterns Skill for one bounded shell-script task, then verify it produces useful guidance and integrates with the existing Rules.
suggestions.validation: Confirm the Skill fires on the task trigger, produces the expected procedure, and does not conflict with the AGENTS.md conventions.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md provides comprehensive navigation, the OpenSpec workflow defines spec-driven development, and 25 architecture docs plus 34 spec files give agents strong context routing.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: npm scripts and Docker Compose cover setup and operation, while permission boundaries remain partly implicit with no doctor or preflight command.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: 36 test files and Jest scripts exist for unit and E2E validation, but no hook, CI, or required gate enforces checks before acceptance.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: Docker Compose supports deployment, but no acceptance boundary, approval gate, or owned rollback route is visible for agent-produced changes.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: Six Skills and normalized event infrastructure exist, but zero episode records and zero observed invocations prevent any reuse or improvement claim.

findings.title: Quality gates are documented but not mechanically enforced
findings.reason: AGENTS.md documents lint, test, and format commands, and 36 test files exist, but no pre-commit hook, CI pipeline, or branch protection enforces them. The project explicitly states it does not use git hooks. Any agent or developer can skip validation without consequence.
expectedOutput: A pre-commit hook or CI check that runs lint and tests on relevant changes.
Confirmation that a failing check blocks acceptance.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Add the smallest mechanical enforcement (pre-commit hook or CI check) that runs lint and tests before acceptance, while keeping the existing validation commands.

## Validation

- Confirm the hook or CI triggers on the relevant change path
- Verify it blocks acceptance when checks fail
- Ensure existing test and lint commands remain usable

findings.title: No verifiable acceptance boundary for agent-produced changes
findings.reason: Docker Compose and an entrypoint script support deployment, but there is no CI pipeline, PR requirement, protected branch, or review gate that binds an agent-produced change to a validated acceptance decision. Changes move from workspace to deployment without a verifiable checkpoint.
expectedOutput: A CI check or review requirement that produces a revision-bound acceptance decision before deployment.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Add one owned acceptance gate (CI check or required review) between the workspace change and deployment, preserving the existing Docker deployment route.

## Validation

- Confirm the gate triggers on changes targeting the deployment path
- Verify it produces a pass or fail decision bound to the revision
- Ensure the Docker deployment route remains functional

findings.title: Configured Skills are not routed to agent task work
findings.reason: Six project Skills are configured with triggers and procedures (five of six have trigger, procedure, and validation present), but none are routed to any observed agent task. They exist as static assets without activation through task routing, so their guidance never reaches the agent during work.
expectedOutput: At least one configured Skill routed to a task type with confirmed activation.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Route the highest-value configured Skill (bash-defensive-patterns or nestjs-best-practices) to a bounded task type, preserving existing Rules.

## Validation

- Confirm the Skill activates on the task trigger
- Verify it produces the expected procedure and output
- Ensure it does not conflict with AGENTS.md conventions

findings.title: No mechanism captures repeated work or lifecycle opportunities
findings.reason: The project has zero episode records, zero recurring candidates, and zero scoped Skill observations. Without normalized lifecycle events, the Harness cannot distinguish repeated work, route verified demand into reusable improvements, or maintain an intervention ledger. Repeated tasks remain invisible to the learning loop.
expectedOutput: Non-zero episode records and recurring candidate detection for the project workspace.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-loop fix this issue

Enable normalized task events for the project workspace so that episode records and recurring candidates become observable.

## Validation

- Confirm at least one episode record appears after a bounded task
- Verify recurring candidates are detected when the same task type repeats
- Ensure the learning observation coverage moves from zero to at least one scoped observation
